questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.**

The lawyer had presented the facts of the case well.

options.text: The facts of the case had presented the lawyer well.
The facts of the case had been presented well by the lawyer.
The facts of the case were being presented by the lawyer well.
The lawyer was presented well by the facts of the case.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2 i.e. The facts of the case had been presented well by the lawyer.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In **active** voice, a sentence emphasizes the subject, performing an action.
 
• In **passive**** voice, **a sentence emphasizes the action or the object of the sentence.
 
• The given sentence is in **Active voice **and it is in **past perfect tense.**
 
• **Active Format:**
 
 
• **​Subject + had + 3rd form of verb + Object **
 
 
 
• **​Passive format:**
 
 
• **Object + had + been + 3rd form of verb + by + subject**
 
 
 
• Hence the correct answer is **option 2.**

 

**​**The correct sentence is: **The facts of the case had been presented well by the lawyer.**

questions.question:
**Complete the collocation.**

Since I like him a lot, I _____ him out.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 3 i.e. asked.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• We use **since** with a point in time in the past. 
 
• The meaning of '**ask out' **is **invite someone out on a date.**
 
• From the word **like **in the first part of the sentence, it is clear that **asked** is the correct option.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is Option 3.

**Correct Sentence:**__ *Since I like him a lot, I **__asked__ **him out.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Talk** **out** means discuss something thoroughly in order to solve a problem or reach a conclusion.
 
• **Go out **means to leave the place where you live or work for a short time, returning on the same day.
 
• **Call out **means summon someone to deal with an emergency or provide a service.
 
• What is a **collocation**?
 
 
• A **collocation **is two or more words that often go together. These combinations just sound "right" to native English speakers, who use them all the time.
 
• **Examples**: a quick shower, a quick meal, a hard frost etc.
